confidence-interval.def: A range of values for a parameter, built as statistic ± (critical value)(standard error). For one proportion, the one-sample z interval is $\hat{p} \pm z^*\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})}{n}}$.

standard-error.def: An estimate of a statistic's standard deviation computed from the sample, used when the parameter in the formula is unknown. For a proportion's interval, $\text{SE} = \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})}{n}}$.

critical-value.def: The multiplier $z^*$ in a confidence interval: the standard normal value with the confidence level's area between $-z^*$ and $z^*$. It is 1.645 for 90%, 1.96 for 95% and 2.576 for 99%.

margin-of-error.def: How far a confidence interval reaches on each side of the point estimate: $\text{ME} = z^* \cdot \text{SE}$. A larger sample makes it smaller; a higher confidence level makes it larger.

conditions.def: What must be true for an inference method to work, checked in words with numbers: random (a random sample or random assignment), 10% (when sampling without replacement), and a shape condition such as large counts.

confidence-level.def: The success rate of the method that builds a confidence interval: for 95% confidence, about 95% of intervals built from many random samples capture the parameter. It sets the critical value.
